answer: Pin each agent to one signed GPS fix. The phone's secure enclave signs its coordinates, and the network keeps only the hash. First, the agent posts a fresh fix at registration. Second, no two agents may sit within 500 metres of each other. Third, a random quarterly recheck demands a new signed fix in ten minutes, and a miss burns a 250 POA bond and freezes the identity 30 days. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 phones in 1,000 places, $150,000 plus travel. At the nadir of trust, one room pretends to be a thousand agents, but each fix is an opal at a narrow inlet, and only one agent passes.
